entries.name: Chemist
entries.flavor: The Chemist is a daring scientist, blending alchemy and medical inventions to push the boundaries of nature itself. Whether concocting potent mixtures or mutating their own form, Chemists are known for their ability to reshape reality through chemical mastery. They are visionaries who weild the power of chemistry to both heal and destroy.
entries.quote: NOTHING IS IMPOSSIBLE FOR A MAN WITH A SKULL FLAG! ISN’T THAT RIGHT? DOCTOR! --- Tony Tony Chopper
startingEquipment: (a) a shield or (b) any simple weapon
(a) a scimitar or (b) any simple melee weapon Thick shirt, an explorer’s pack, and alchemist’s supplies

subclassIntro.text: All chemists spend a majority of their time studying various fields of science to incorporate into their own research. Which other field you decide to specialize in may depend on if you prefer more monstrous transformations, greater invention powers, or the ability to support your allies with chemical conconctions.

features.name: Alchemical Symbols
features.text: You understand how to read alchemical symbols written in ancient blueprints or advanced technology. These symbols are a secret code thought up by the brightest alchemists in the past, and you can quickly and intuitively understand their secret meaning. You and others who know this language automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message’s presence with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check but can’t decipher it without special powers.

features.name: Invention Power (Spellcasting)
features.text: Drawing on the divine essence of chemical composition and alchemy, you can use various invention powers (spells) to shape that essence to your will. Invention Powers are the equivalent of “Spells” in 5th edition, and invention power slots are the same as “Spell Slots”. Make sure to view the “Casting a Spell” section in the Player’s Handbook for understanding Spellcasting in 5th Edition D&D. Chemist creation powers count as Chemist Spells in Chapter 4.

sections.name: Natural Abilities (Cantrips)
sections.text: At 1st level, you know two natural abilities (cantrips) of your choice from the chemist spell list in Chapter 1. You learn additional chemist cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the natural abilities (Cantrips) Known column of the Chemist table.

sections.name: Preparing and Casting Invention Powers (Spells)
sections.text:
The Chemist table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your chemist invention powers (spells) of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these chemist spells, you must expend a slot of the spell’s level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
You prepare the list of chemist invention powers (spells) that are available for you to cast, choosing from the chemist spell list. When you do so, choose a number of chemist spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your Chemist level (minimum of one spell) to add to your chemist invention powers. The spells must be of a level for which you have invention power slots.
For example, if you are a 3rd-level chemist, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level invention power slots. With a Wisdom of 16, your list of prepared invention powers can include six invention powers of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination. If you prepare the 1st-level invention power (spell) Cure Wounds, you can cast it using a 1st-level or 2nd-level slot. Casting the invention power doesn’t remove it from your list of prepared invention powers. You can also change your list of prepared invention powers (spells) when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of chemist invention powers requires time spent in deep study: at least 1 minute per invention power level for each invention power on your list.

sections.name: Invention (Spellcasting) Ability
sections.text:
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your chemist invention powers (spells), since your power draws upon your devotion and attunement to chemistry and science. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a chemist invention power you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Invention save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Invention attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

sections.name: Ritual Casting
sections.text: You can cast a chemist invention power (spell) as a ritual if that invention power (spell) has the ritual tag and you have the invention power prepared.

sections.name: Invention (Spellcasting) Focus
sections.text: You can use a alchemist’s supplies as a spellcasting focus for your chemist Invention powers.

features.name: Monster Mutation
features.text:
Starting at 2nd level, using a chemical concoction to alter your lineage factor, you can use your action to transform yourself into an abomination using the stat block below. You can use this feature twice. You regain expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.
You can stay in your abomination form for a number of hours equal to half your chemist level (rounded down). You then revert to your normal form unless you expend another use of this feature. You can revert to your normal form earlier by using a bonus action on your turn. You automatically revert if you fall unconscious, drop to 0 hit points, or die.
While you are transformed, the following rules apply:
Choose 1 Statistical Splice and 2 Morph Splices from the abomination splices area at the end of your class/subclass descriptions. You can choose new splices when you re-enter your abomination form each time.
Your abomination’s Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores are 20, 16, and 14. You can assign each number to the ability score of your choice.
Your proficiency bonus is equal to your characters while in this form.
Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the abomination, but you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. If the creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block is higher than yours, use the creature’s bonus instead of yours. If the creature has any legendary or lair actions, you can’t use them.
When you transform, you assume the abomination’s hit points and Hit Dice. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form, For example, if you take 10 damage in animal form and have only 1 hit point left, you revert and take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn’t reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren’t knocked unconscious.
If a splice has a damage dice roll in the feature or an associated attack, the damage is increase by 1 additional dice at 5th level, 10th level, 15th level, and 20th level.
You can’t cast special powers (spells) while in your abomination form. Transforming doesn’t break your concentration on a special power (spell) you’ve already cast, however, or prevent you from taking actions that are part of a special power (spell), such as Call Lightning, that you’ve already cast.
If you have Devil Fruit powers, you cannot use them while in this form, as your lineage factor is temporarily disrupted. This includes all devil fruit curse effects as well. If you eat a devil fruit while in your abomination form, you gain the powers. However as soon as you transform back into your normal form, you instantly die as if you had eaten 2 devil fruits.
You retain the benefit of any features already cast from your class, race, or other source and can use them if the new form is physically capable of doing so.
You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space or merges into your new form. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.

rows: Hit Points (10 + your chemist level) x 2
Claws. Melee Weapon Attack: +0 to hit, reach 5ft., one target.

features.name: Chemist Study
features.text: At 2nd level, you choose to study an additional field of science alongside chemistry, incorporating the two together. Choose Aerostatic, Botany, Cryochemist, Genetics, Medicine, or Pyrochemist, all detailed at the end of the class description. Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two Ability Scores of your choice by 1. Alternatively, you can take a feat listed in Chapter 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Additionally, whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace one natural ability (cantrip) you learned from this class’s Invention Power (Spellcasting) feature with another cantrip from the chemist spell list.

features.name: Immortality Research
features.text: Starting at 18th level, the chemical knowledge that you possess allows you to develop medicine that makes you to age more slowly. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year. This medicine only works on you.

features.name: Abomination Powers
features.text: Beginning at 18th level, you can cast many of your invention powers (spells) in any shape you assume using your Monster Mutation. You can perform the somatic and verbal components of a invention power while in an abomination form, but you aren’t able to provide material components.

features.name: Perfected Mutation
features.text:
At 20th level, you can use your Monster Mutation an unlimited number of times.
Additionally, you can ignore the verbal and somatic components of your chemist invention powers (spells), as well as any material components that lack a cost and aren’t consumed by a invention power (spell). You gain this benefit in both your normal shape and your abomination form.

entries.name: Aerostatics
entries.flavor: Prepare airborne concoctions that strengthen allies and weaken foes by utilizing the power of volatile chemicals that fill the air with magical effects. These concoctions float through the battlefield, turning the tide in your favor with lingering mists and clouds that impact those within.

features.name: Vaporous Concoctions
features.text:
Starting at 2nd level, you can create airborne chemical mixtures that affect the battlefield. As an action, you can throw a flask of vaporous concoction to a point within 30 feet, creating a 10-foot-radius cloud of gas that lasts for 1 minute. The cloud is embued following effects:
Allies who enter for the first time on their turn or start their turn in the area within the cloud gain temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Wisdom modifier.
Enemies within the cloud have disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws until the end of their next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses after a long rest.

features.name: Chemical Splicing
features.text: Also at 2nd level, when choosing morph splices for your abomination form, you may also choose from the Aerostatic Morph Splices list. If you choose a aerostatic splice your abomination form gains resistance to poison and acid damage and the poison condition.

features.name: Reactive Atmosphere
features.text:
At 6th level, your airborne concoctions become more volatile. You can use your reaction to trigger one of the following effects at any time:
Hastening Mist: Shepard allies out of danger, allowing all allies within the clouds to move up to 15 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. Enduring Smog: All allies within the clouds gains a +2 bonus to AC until the end of their next turn. Gasous Adrenaline: All allies within the clouds gains an additional action on their next turn. That action can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.
Revitalizing Cloud All allies within the clouds regains 1 hit point.
Choking Haze: Force all enemies inside the clouds to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier) or be stunned until the end of their next turn. If an enemy succeeds, they are immune from this effect for 24 hours.
Blinding Gas: Enemies within the clouds have disadvantage on their first attack roll until the end of their next turn.
Corrosive Dew: Acidic dew clinges to enemy armor. Enemies within the clouds have a -2 AC until the start of your next turn.
Poisonious Vapor: All creatures within the clouds take an amount of poison damage equal to your chemist level + your wisdom modifier.
You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

features.name: Lingering Toxins
features.text:
At 10th level, the effects of your vaporous concoctions heighten and linger even after the cloud disperses. When you create a vaporous concoction cloud, it is enhanced with the following effect along with all original effects:
Allies who enter or start their turn in the area gain advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed.
Enemies who enter or start their turn in the area have their speed halved until the end of their next turn.
Additionally, when one of your vaporous clouds ends, it leaves behind the residual effects listed above in the area for 1 minute.

features.name: Aerostatic Mastery
features.text: At 14th level, you have perfected the art of controlling airborne concoctions. The radius of your clouds increases to 20 feet, and they now last for 10 minutes instead of 1 minute. You can also choose to make one cloud invisible.

entries.name: Botany
entries.flavor: Botanists will often focus on the landscape and plantlife in foreign lands, enabling greater innovations and herbal remedies or concotions.

features.name: Bonus Natural Ability (Cantrip)
features.text: When you choose this study at 2nd level, you learn one additional chemist cantrip of your choice. This cantrip doesn’t count against the number of chemist natural abilities (cantrips) you know.

features.name: Herbal Remedy
features.text:
Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your creative energy by consuming herbal concotions you’ve prepared from gathering special local plants. During a short rest, you choose expended invention power slots to recover. The invention power slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your chemist level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You can’t use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
For example, when you are a 4th-level chemist, you can recover up to two levels worth of invention power slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level slot or two 1st- level slots.

features.name: Flora Splicing
features.text: Also at 2nd level, when choosing morph splices for your abomination form, you may also choose from the Botany Morph Splices list. If you choose a botany splice your abomination form gains 2 hit points when they land a successful attack against a creature.

features.name: Field Invention Powers (Spells)
features.text:
Your deep connection and understading of nature and plantlife enables you to advance your research far beyond ordinary levels. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to special invention powers depending on the plantlife in the region you primarily study. Choose that land – arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or underground – and consult the associated list of invention powers.
Once you gain access to a field invention power, you always have it prepared, and it doesn’t count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a invention power (spell) that doesn’t appear on the chemist spell list, the spell is nonetheless a chemist invention power for you.

rows: Commune with Nature, Cone of Cold
Create Food and Water, Protection from Energy

features.name: Nature’s Step
features.text:
Starting at 6th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such as those created by the Entangle spell.

features.name: Botanist’s Antidote
features.text: When you reach 10th level, you can’t be charmed or frightened and you are immune to poison and disease.

effects.label: Can’t be charmed or frightened; immune to poison and disease

features.name: Natural Repellent
features.text:
When you reach 14th level, you develop plant-based fragrances that make wild creatures hesitant to attack you. When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your chemist invention save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours.
The creature is aware of this effect before it makes its attack against you.

entries.name: Cryochemist
entries.flavor: Tap into the primal power of ice and snow, transforming into a fearsome Yeti to overwhelm foes and protect allies.

features.name: Icy Fortitude
features.text:
Starting at 2nd level, you can enhance yourself or an ally with a surge of icy resilience. As a bonus action, you touch a willing creature and grant them temporary hit points equal to your Chemist level + your Wisdom modifier. Additionally, the affected creature becomes coated in a thin layer of frost, which chills any attacker.
For the duration of these temporary hit points, any creature that hits the target with a melee attack takes cold damage equal to your Wisdom modifier and is slowed by 10 ft until the end of their next turn.
You may not use this feature on a target that has icy fortitude active on themself. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses after a long rest.

features.name: Cryochemical Splicing
features.text: Also at 2nd level, when choosing morph splices for your abomination form, you may also choose from the Cryochemist Morph Splices list. If you choose a cryochemist splice your abomination form gains resistance to cold damage.

features.name: Partial Yeti Transformation
features.text:
At 6th level, you can partially transform into a Yeti, growing a thick layer of icy fur and gaining some of the creature’s strength. As a bonus action, you can enter your Partial Yeti Transformation, which lasts for 10 minutes or until you end it as a bonus action. While transformed, you gain the following benefits:
Icy Resilience: You gain temporary hit points equal to your Chemist level + your Wisdom modifier.
Frost Strike: Your unarmed strikes deal an additional 1d6 cold damage, and any creature hit by your unarmed strikes has its speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of your next turn.
Cold Resistance: You gain resistance to cold damage.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Full Yeti Transformation
features.text:
At 10th level, you can fully transform into a Yeti, taking on its monstrous form to unleash your full icy potential. As an action, you can transform into a Yeti Form for up to 1 hour or until you end the transformation as a bonus action. While in this form, you gain the following benefits as well as all benefits from the partial yeti transformation feature:
Yeti Strength: You gain advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, and your unarmed strikes deal 1d8 + your Strength modifier cold damage.
Chilling Presence: As an action, you can unleash a chilling roar that forces all creatures within 15 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Chemist spell save DC or be frightened and slowed by 10 ft. until the start of your next turn.
Icy Breath: As an action, you can exhale a cone of icy wind in a 15-foot cone. Creatures in the area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 4d6 cold damage on a failed save and having their speed reduced to 0 until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, they take half damage and are not slowed.
Once you use Full Yeti Transformation, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Frostbound Titan
features.text:
At 14th level, you perfect your transformation, becoming a true embodiment of winter’s fury. When you use your Full Yeti Transformation, you gain the following additional benefits:
Enlarge: Your size doubles in all dimensions, and your weight is multiplied by eight. This growth increases your size by one category. Your unarmed melee attacks deal an extra 1d4 damage.
Icebound Resilience: You gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks while in your Yeti Form.
Avalanche Charge: When you move at least 20 feet straight towards a creature and hit it with a melee attack, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Invention save DC or be knocked prone and take an additional 2d6 cold damage.
Frozen Aura: You emanate an aura of intense cold in a 10-foot radius, causing the ground and all surfaces to form slick ice, turning it into difficult terrain for the duration. When the ice appears, each creature other than you standing in its area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. A creature that enters the area on it’s own or ends its turn there must also succeed on a Dexterity saving equal to your Invention save DC throw or fall prone.
You can maintain your Full Yeti Transformation for up to 1 hour or until you end it as a bonus action, and you can use it once per long rest.

entries.name: Genetics
entries.flavor: This field of science allows those who study it to heavily modify lineage factors and the genetics of living creatures. Geneticists are capable of creating a new level of mutations in their subjects.

features.name: Combat Mutation
features.text:
When you choose this study at 2nd level, you gain the ability to use Monster Mutation on your turn as a bonus action, rather than as an action.
Additionally, while you are transformed by your Monster Mutation, you can use a bonus action to expend one invention power (spell) slot to regain 1d8 hit points per level of the invention power slot expended.

features.name: Unstable Mutation
features.text:
The study of your field grants you the ability to manipulate your abominations DNA at will. Starting at 2nd level, as an action while in your abomination form, you can switch any number of your morph splices out with new ones.
Additionally, you gain 1 additional statistical and morph splice when transforming.

features.name: Monsterous Strikes
features.text: Starting at 6th level, your attacks in abomination form count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

features.name: Elemental Mutation
features.text: At 10th level, you can expend two uses of Monster Mutation at the same time to transform into an air elemental, an earth elemental, a fire elemental, or a water elemental instead of an abomination.

features.name: Thousand Mutations
features.text:
By 14th level, you have learned to enhance your abomination form further. You gain 1 additional morph splice feature when you transform.
Additionally, you can pick from any other subclasses splices when choosing your morph splices.

entries.name: Medicine
entries.flavor: The field of medicine allows scientists to develop a wide variety of synthetic and natural remedies alike to treat and heal those in need.

features.name: Pharmacist
features.text: At 2nd level, you learn how to develop beneficial medicines to cure aliments and save lives. You can craft medicines during a long rest using Alchemist Supplies. You can craft a number of medications up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one), with each medicine requires a specific crafting cost to create.

sections.name: Medicine Table
sections.text: All medicines can be found in Chapter 9: Medical Log

features.name: Medical Tent
features.text:
At 6th level, through your study of field medics, you’ve learned how to set up advanced tents that guard your comrades while they rest inside. During a short or long rest, you can set up a sensor that detects intruders up to a 30-foot-radius around the tent where your allies rest.
While in the sensor’s radius, you and your allies gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) and Wisdom (Perception) checks, and any light from open flames in the radius (a campfire, torches, or the like) isn’t visible outside the radius
The sensor vanishes at the end of the rest or when you leave the radius.

features.name: Abomination Potion
features.text:
Also at 6th level, you find a new but highly unorthodox treatment for your allies. As an action, give a willing creature a hastily made abomination concoction. Grant an creature 1 Statistical Splice and 1 non-subclass Morph Splice of your choice for 1 minute.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you have taken a short or long rest.

features.name: Instant Rescue
features.text:
Starting at 10th level, you develop technology that allows you to blink over to a different point in space. As a bonus action on your turn, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, you can use your action to teleport one willing creature you touch up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Brain Imaging
features.text:
At 14th level, you develop a brain imaging device that allows you to be able to enter dreams and use special powers.
When you finish a short rest, you can cast one of the following invention powers (spells), without expending a invention power slot or requiring material components: Dream (with you as the messenger) and Scrying
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Pyrochemist
entries.flavor: Delve into the destructive power of fire, harnessing volatile chemicals to unleash searing heat. Turn yourself into a living blaze, boosting their own damage output at the cost of burning yourself, making them masters of risky, high-stakes combat.

features.name: Immolation Surge
features.text:
Starting at 2nd level, you can heat your body to extreme temperatures, turning yourself into a walking inferno. As a bonus action, you activate Immolation Surge, which lasts for 1 minute or until you end it as a bonus action. While Immolation Surge is active, you gain the following effects:
Blazing Aura: Creatures that start their turn within 5 feet of you take fire damage equal to your Chemist level.
Enhanced Damage: Your melee attacks, fire-based spells, and pryochemist features deal an additional 1d6 fire damage.
Self-Immolation: At the start of each of your turns, you take fire damage equal to half your Chemist level (rounded up).
You may end immolation surge with a bonus action.

features.name: Pyrochemical Splicing
features.text: Also at 2nd level, when choosing morph splices for your abomination form, you may also choose from the Pyrochemist Morph Splices list. If you choose a pyrochemist splice your abomination form gains resistance to fire damage.

features.name: Firebombs
features.text:
At 6nd level, you can craft volatile firebombs that create fiery explosions. As an action, you can throw a firebomb at a point you can see within 30 feet exploding in a 10- foot radius. Creatures in the radius must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Chemist spell save DC, taking 3d6 fire damage on a failed save and half damage on a success.
The damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 10th level (4d6), and 14th level (5d6).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses after a short or long rest.

features.name: Ignition Burst
features.text:
At 10th level, you can unleash a burst of fiery energy from your body when struck. When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to release an Ignition Burst, dealing 3d6 fire damage to the attacker and all creatures within 5 feet of you. Creatures in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw or take full damage; on a successful save, they take half damage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses after a long rest.

features.name: Volcanic Eruption
features.text:
At 14th level, you unleash the pinnacle of your destructive capabilities with a massive explosion. As an action, you create an Explosion at a point you can see within 60 feet, causing a violent burst of flame in a 30- foot radius. Creatures in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Chemist spell save DC. On a failed save, they take 8d6 fire damage and are knocked prone. On a successful save, they take half damage and are not knocked prone.
You can use this feature once per long rest.

options.name: Health Enhancement
options.text: Double your abomination form’s hit points.

options.name: Improve Quality
options.text: Choose two ability scores from Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution. Increase those ability scores by an amount equal to your wisdom modifier.

options.name: Retain Mind
options.text: You can use all chemist spells you know while transformed as your abomination.

options.name: Tough Body
options.text: Increase your abomination’s AC by +2.

options.name: Additional Appendages
options.text:
Your abomination form grows two slightly smaller secondary arms below your primary pair of arms. The secondary arms can manipulate an object, open or close a door or container, pick up or set down a medium or smaller object, or use the bleeding claw attack as a bonus action.
Bleeding Claws. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5ft., one target. Hit: (1) piercing damage. When a creature takes damage from this attack then gain 1 stack of bleed. At the beginning of each turn, a creature with bleed takes an amount of necrotic damage equal to the current bleed stack amount. A creature can use an action to remove all stacks of bleed from themselves.

options.name: Aquatic Hunter
options.text:
Your abomination form adapts to survive in aquatic environments. The abomination form can breathe both air and water, gains a swimming speed equal to it’s walking speed, and gains the bite attack.
Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5ft., one target. Hit: (1d10 + your Strength modifier) piercing damage. The abomination attaches to the target. While attached, the abomination can’t attack, and at the start of each of the abomination’s turns, the target takes 6 (1d12) necrotic damage. The attached abomination moves with the target whenever the target moves, requiring none of the abomination’s movement. The abomination can detach itself by spending 5 feet of its movement on its turn. A creature, including the target, can use its action to detach the abomination.

options.name: Bite-Sized
options.text: Your abomination form shrinks to a more manageable size. You can choose to be medium, small, or tiny sized and you can move through hostile tokens if you are at least 1 size smaller then the creature.

options.name: Carapace Growth
options.text:
Your abomination grows armored plates along it’s back. The abomination gain +2 AC. Additionally, when you use the dodge action gain +3 AC until the start of you next turn.
Additionally, opportunity attacks against your are rolled with disadvantage.

options.name: Clambering Adaptation
options.text:
Your abomination form adapts to climbing vertical and upside down surfaces. Gain a climbing speed equal to your abominations walking speed.
Additionally, when the abomination falls, it can move 5 ft. horizontally for every 10 feet it falls vertically, up to a maximum distance equal to their walking speed per turn.

options.name: Enlarged Spines
options.text:
The abomination grows spines across it’s body. When a hostile creature attacks you with a melee attack and it hits, the creature takes 1d6 piercing damage. Additionally, you learn the spine launcher attack.
Spike Launcher. Ranged Weapon Attack: reach 25/50ft., one target. Hit: (1d6 + your Dexterity modifier) piercing damage.

options.name: Frenzy
options.text:
The abomination can make two melee attacks on it’s turn as an action.
Additionally, the abomination can spend a bonus action to go into frenzy mode, gaining advantage on all attacks until the beginning of their next turn. While frenzied all attacks against the abomination are rolled with advantage.

options.name: Great Maw
options.text:
Your abomination grows an appetite big enough to swallow a horse. The abomination can make a big bite attack against a target.
Big Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: (1d10 + your Strength modifier) piercing damage. If the target has a token size smaller than the abomination and the attack hits, the target is swallowed. The swallowed target is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the abomination, and it takes 3 (1d6) acid damage at the start of each of the abominations’s turns. The abomination can have only one target swallowed at a time. If the abomination form ends, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and is placed in the nearest unoccupied space within 5 ft. of it, exiting prone.

options.name: Gore Charger
options.text:
Your abomination form grows a horns from its head. If the abomination moves at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and then hits it with a gore attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a Strength saving throw equal to your Invention save DC or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the abomination can make one stomp attack against it as a bonus action.
Gore. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5ft., one target. Hit: (1d8 + your Strength modifier) piercing damage.
Stomp. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5ft., one target. Hit: (1d10 + your Strength modifier) bludgeoning damage.

options.name: Hugeify
options.text:
Your abomination form grows and their muscles bulge with titanic strength. Your size grows to huge and your melee attacks deal an extra 1d10 damage, dealing double damage to structures and objects. While in this form your can carry five times your normal carry weight.
Additionally, you can dislodge large rocks from the ground to throw at your enemies.
Rock. Melee Weapon Attack: throw 30/120 ft., one target. Hit: (1d10 + your Strength modifier) bludgeoning damage.

options.name: Isolationist
options.text: The abomination has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if their are no allies within 60 ft. of the creature.

options.name: Nocturnal Predator
options.text: Your abomination form adapts to pitch darkness. It gains 120 ft. of darkvision, seeing in shades of grey, and it has advantage on attack rolls while in darkness. If you are in dim or bright light, you do not gain advantage on your attack rolls.

options.name: Pack Beast
options.text: The abomination has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the abomination’s allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and the ally isn’t incapacitated.

options.name: Pounce Enhancement
options.text:
Your abomination form’s leg muscles are enhanced. As a bonus action, the abomination can jump a number of feet equal to five times your proficiency bonus, without provoking opportunity attacks.
Additionally, if the abomination moves at least 30 feet straight toward a creature (through walking or jumping) and then hits it with an attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a Strength saving throw equal to your Invention save DC or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the abomination can make one melee attack against it for free.

options.name: Sky Ward
options.text:
Your abomination form grows large wings. Gain a fly speed equal to your abominations walking speed and gains the talons attack.
Talons. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5ft., one target. Hit: (1d6 + your Strength modifier) piercing damage.

options.name: Sprint Burst
options.text:
Your abomination forms digitigrade legs able to sprint long distances. Double the abominations walking speed and when they make a melee attack against a creature, they don’t provoke opportunity attacks from that creature for the rest of the turn, whether the abomination hit or not. You also gain the kick attack.
Kick. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5ft., one target. Hit: (1d6 + your Strength modifier) bludgeoning damage.

options.name: Stalker
options.text: The abomination can change its coloration to match its surroundings. It doesn’t need cover to attempt to Hide with a Stealth check and it’s stealth is increased by half of your chemist level.

options.name: Subterranean Beast
options.text:
Your abomination form adapts to moving underground. Gain a burrow speed equal to your abominations walking speed.
Additionally, if you are currently underground, you can use an bonus action to move up to 30 ft. and erupt from beneath a target. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw equal to your Invention save DC or take 1d10 bludgeoing damage and knocked prone into a new unoccupied space within 5 ft. of the abomination. If the target succeeds on their save the abomination cannot burrow again until the start of their next turn.

options.name: Tracker
options.text:
Your abomination form’s senses enhance, allowing you to track creatures with ease. The abomination has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing, smell, or sight.
Additionally, if you are looking for a creature and find it’s tracks . You know the creatures locations at all times if they are within 1 mile of your location.

options.name: Venomous Striker
options.text:
Your abomination form grows a long segmented tail and stinger gaining the sting attack.
Sting. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5ft., one target. Hit: (1d6 + your Strength modifier) piercing damage, and the target must make a Constitution saving throw equal to your Invention save DC, taking 5 (1d10) poison damage and becoming poisoned for 1d4 minutes on a failed save, or half as much damage and not poisoned on a successful save. Once a creature succeeds on a saving throw against being poisoned, they are immune to your stingers poison for 24 hours.

options.name: Acidic Claws
options.text:
Your abomination form’s claws begin to drip acid from its pores. Gain the acid claws attack.
Acid Claws. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5ft., one target. Hit: (1d6) acid damage. The targets AC is reduced by -1 for 1 minute. This effect can stack up to -5 AC.

options.name: Adhesive Spit
options.text:
Your abomination’s mouth begins to secrete sticky goo instead of saliva. Gain the adhesive spit attack.
Adhesive Spit (Recharge 5-6). Ranged Weapon Attack: reach 20/40ft., one target. Hit: The target is restrained by goo. Using half of its movement speed, the restrained target can make a Strength check equal to your Invention save DC, freeing itself from the sticky goo on a success.

options.name: Toxin Breath
options.text: Your abomination form gains the ability to exhale fire from it’s throat. As an action, the abomination exhales a noxious cloud in a 10-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw equal to your Invention save DC, becoming paralyzed for 1 minute on a failed save. The target can make the save again at the beginning of each of its turns. The creature becomes immune to the paralysis for 24 hours if they succeed on any of the saving throws.

options.name: Venomous Jaws
options.text:
Your abominations jaws grow stronger and it grows venomous fangs. Gain the venomous bite attack and when you successfully land a bite, you grapple the target. At the beginning of each turn, deal (1d10) automatic poison damage to the grappled target. You cannot bite again until you or the target ends the grapple.
Venomous Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5ft., one target. Hit: (1d6 + your Strength modifier) piercing damage, and the target must make a Constitution saving throw equal to your Invention save DC, taking 5 (1d10) poison damage and becoming poisoned for 1d4 minutes on a failed save, or half as much damage and not poisoned on a successful save.

options.name: Floral Regeneration
options.text: Your abomination is infused with DNA that allows it’s body to regenerate from damage. At the beginning of each turn heal 1d4 hit points.

options.name: Serpent Vines
options.text: You infuse your abomination with vine DNA giving it the ability to morph their arms into expanding vines. As a bonus action, the abomination’s arm turns into a vine that extends from it’s body. The abomination can lash out at a creature within 30 feet of it that it can see. That creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw equal to your Invention save DC or be dragged 20 ft. in a direction of the abomination’s choosing, even dragging the creature out of the 30 ft. range.

options.name: Sleep Pollen
options.text:
Your abomination is infused with the ability to disperse pollen from it’s body. As an action, select a point within 60 ft. and roll a 5d8; the total is how many hit points of creatures this pollen can affect. Creatures within 20 feet of a point you choose within range are affected in ascending order of their current hit points (ignoring unconscious creatures). Starting with the creature that has the lowest current hit points, each creature affected by the pollen falls unconscious until the spell ends, the sleeper takes damage, or someone uses an action to shake or slap the sleeper awake. Subtract each creature’s hit points from the total before moving on to the creature with the next lowest hit points. A creature’s hit points must be equal to or less than the remaining total for that creature to be affected.
Additionally, when you gain 3d8 additional dice at 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th levels.

options.name: Sun Petals
options.text: Your abomination form sprouts life during combat. When you cast a spell that requires spell slots in your abomination form, you leave behind a single sun petal flower on your space. If a creature eats this flower with a bonus action, they gain (1d6 x spell level cast) hit point. This spell is not effected by the dice increases at 5th, 10th, 15th, or 20th levels.

options.name: Cryo Breath
options.text:
Your abomination form gains the ability to exhale frigid winds from it’s mouth. As an action, the abomination exhales fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw equal to your Invention save DC, taking (1d4) cold damage and slowed by 10 ft. on a failed save.
Additionally, as an action, you may breath permafrost on a weapon. The weapon’s damage is increased by an additional 1d6 cold damage for 1 minute.

options.name: Frigid Aura
options.text: A constant mist of frozen air erupts from your abominations body. The first time a creature enters a space or starts within 5 ft. of the abomination on a turn, that creature takes 2 (1d4) cold damage and their movement speed is reduced by 10 ft.

options.name: Frozen Trail
options.text:
Wherever your abomination goes, never-ending frost follows. Wherever the abomination travels, it leaves behind a layer of frost, making the ground difficult terrain until the start of it’s next turn. You are not affected by your own frozen trail.
Additionally, you may walk on liquid as it freezes beneath your feet.

options.name: Icicle Tomb
options.text:
The abomination grows giant icicles down it’s spine. You learn the icicle javelin attack.
Icicle Javelin. Ranged Weapon Attack: reach 30/60ft., one target. Hit: (1d4) cold damage. If a target is hit, reduce its movement speed by 5 ft. until the end of your next turn. If you land additional javelins, the targets movement speed is reduced by 5 ft. per attack, resetting the timer. If the targets movement speed is reduced by 20 ft. they are encased in an icy tomb, restraining them until the start of your next turn. When they emerge, all icicle javelin movement effects are removed.

options.name: Fire Breath
options.text: Your abomination form gains the ability to exhale fire from it’s throat. As an action, the abomination exhales fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw equal to your Invention save DC, taking (2d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

options.name: Heat Mane
options.text: A mane of fire ignites along the abominations spine. The first time a creature enters a space or starts within 5 ft. of the abomination on a turn, that creature takes 3 (1d6) fire damage.

options.name: Molten Claws
options.text:
Your abomination’s claws crack and break as lava begins to drip out of them. Gain the molten claws attack.
Molten Claws. Melee Weapon Attack: reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: (1d8) fire damage. If the target is a creature or a flammable object, it ignites. Until a creature takes an action to douse the fire, the creature takes 3 (1d6) fire damage at the end of each of its turns.

options.name: Molten Eruption
options.text: The abomination slams the ground beneath it, turning stone and soil into a molten explosion. As an action, each creature within 5 ft. of the abomination other than itself must make a Dexterity saving throw equal to your Invention save DC, taking (2d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
